retained_source_evidence.text: Professor Emeritus of the University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF), School of Fisheries and Ocean Sciences (SFOS), Institute of Marine Science (IMS)
PROBES: Processes and Resources Of the eastern Bering Sea shelf

The stimulus for Processes and Resources of the Eastern Bering Sea Shelf (PROBES) was a mutual US - Japan scientific concern about the ability of the Bering Sea to support the huge annual catch, on a sustained basis, of groundfish, pelagic fish, crab and other marine resources.  The question was large enough to demand the attention of oceanographic disciplines from both countries as well as from others.  After several conferences, it was decided to emphasize the "Golden Triangle" (the are encompassed southeastern Bering Sea shelf in an attempt to understand the bioproductivity of this region (Hood and Kelley 1974, Hood and Takenouti 1975).  In the beginning, it appeared most expedient, for logistic and funding reasons, to have each country pursue its part of the program independently.
A report on PROBES: Processes and Resources Of the eastern Bering Sea shelf

capacity_assessment.contact_boundary: Point-of-contact and distribution contact person fields were read as separate metadata roles. They are not evidence authorizing promotion into the creator array or identification of the unnamed credit.
capacity_assessment.role_preservation: Keep the complete Professor Emeritus title and all UAF/SFOS/IMS wording in the literal legacy credit and original context; do not strip the status or infer affiliation fields.

retained_source_evidence.text: Director, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USF&WS)
BERPAC; A program for long-term ecological research of ecosystems of the Bering and Chukchi Seas and the Pacific Ocean

Deterioration of ecosystems on a large scale threatens many functional equilibria in the biosphere.  This problem is particularly urgent for the World Ocean, which is the sink for many different pollutants that can produce significant ecological impacts.  This report is a planning document for BERPAC that discusses marine ecosystems, including biological, physical and biogeochemical cycles.
        [Reference: Turner, J.F., H.J. O'Connor, Y.A. Izrael, and A.V. Tsyban. 1990?. BERPAC : a program for long-term ecological research of ecosystems of the Bering and Chukchi Seas and the Pacific Ocean. National Fund for the Patuxent Wildlife Research Center, 13022 8th Street, Bowie, Maryland 20720. 12 p.]
        This volume may be found at many university libraries.
Planning BERPAC: A program for long-term ecological research of ecosystems of the Bering and Chukchi Seas and the Pacific Ocean.

capacity_assessment.strongest_literal_reading: An agency leadership title whose literal wording can denote either the organizational office or an unnamed person serving in that capacity.
capacity_assessment.organizational_office_reading: Plausible, but not established by the institution-qualified title alone. The XML does not explicitly say Office of the Director or otherwise distinguish corporate issuance from personal authorship.
capacity_assessment.actual_ambiguity_or_gap: The abstract contains a reference for the same BERPAC work naming Turner, J.F.; O'Connor, H.J.; Izrael, Y.A.; and Tsyban, A.V. This is a substantive personal-authorship context. It does not connect any person to the origin or explicitly define the origin as an organizational office.
capacity_assessment.contact_boundary: The separate Turner contact/distribution fields do not establish the origin capacity. No incumbent is identified, no author is substituted, and none of the four bibliographic names is added as a creator.
capacity_assessment.role_preservation: Keep Director and the full U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USF&WS) literal; do not convert Director into an inferred structured role or affiliation, and retain Check with Source use restrictions.
